readings: Using invoices joined to their orders and the customers who placed them, count distinct invoiced orders for each gender represented among those customers, treating missing gender as its own group. Take the unweighted average of those gender counts. For genders whose counts exceed that average, return one row containing the average of their counts and the average amount by which their counts exceed the overall average.

For every gender present in Customers, including missing gender as its own group, count distinct orders that have at least one invoice, assigning zero to any gender with no invoiced orders. Take the unweighted average of those gender counts. For genders whose counts exceed that average, return one row containing the average of their counts and the average amount by which their counts exceed the overall average.
queries:
WITH gender_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count
    FROM Invoices AS i
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
),
overall_average AS (
    SELECT AVG(order_count) AS average_count
    FROM gender_counts
)
SELECT
    AVG(gc.order_count) AS average_count,
    AVG(gc.order_count - oa.average_count) AS average_excess
FROM gender_counts AS gc
CROSS JOIN overall_average AS oa
WHERE gc.order_count > oa.average_count

WITH gender_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender, COUNT(DISTINCT i.order_id) AS order_count
    FROM Customers AS c
    LEFT JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
),
overall AS (
    SELECT AVG(order_count) AS average_count
    FROM gender_counts
)
SELECT
    AVG(g.order_count) AS average_count,
    AVG(g.order_count - o.average_count) AS average_excess
FROM gender_counts AS g
CROSS JOIN overall AS o
WHERE g.order_count > o.average_count
